title: Brightness levels randomly changing every second after using Power Display

judgment.rationale: The report describes a one-second brightness oscillation, but the maintainer already asked for /bugreport and the issue still lacks the diagnostic ZIP plus one confirmation about competing OS/OEM brightness automation.
evidence: The slider visibly jumps between two brightness levels about once per second.
The issue says Power Display content-based brightness was set to On Battery Only even though the machine was plugged in.
Maintainer moooyo asked for /bugreport and no ZIP was added.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the thread waiting on the reporter for a fresh bugreport and adaptive-brightness confirmation.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current evidence cannot yet separate Power Display writes from Windows or OEM brightness automation.

issue_context.summary: Power Display intermittently drives the laptop brightness back and forth every second, but the thread still lacks the bugreport and OS-brightness-state confirmation needed to isolate the owner.
known_information: The visible brightness slider jumps between two levels.
No diagnostic ZIP was attached after the maintainer asked for /bugreport.
inferences: A second brightness controller remains plausible.
If PowerToys owns it, the fault is likely in monitor-brightness coordination rather than the manual slider UI.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter can still provide the exact evidence that distinguishes Power Display from Windows/OEM automation, so the issue should stay in an honest waiting-on-author state.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body and the maintainer /bugreport request.
Reviewed the Power Display module and confirmed logs are needed to distinguish PowerToys writes from external brightness control.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP captured immediately after the oscillation starts.
information_gaps.why_needed: It will show whether Power Display was actively writing brightness at the time the slider was bouncing.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please reproduce the oscillation and then add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward.

information_gaps.information: Whether Windows adaptive brightness, content adaptive brightness control, or an OEM display utility was enabled, and whether the machine was on AC power.
information_gaps.why_needed: That distinguishes a Power Display regression from a second brightness controller outside PowerToys.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please reply with the current Windows/OEM brightness settings and confirm the affected occurrence happened while plugged in.

comment.body:
Thanks for describing that the brightness slider visibly bounces between two values about once per second while Power Display is enabled. Please provide:

1. A fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP captured immediately after the oscillation starts: reproduce the problem and then add a comment containing /bugreport right away.
2. Please confirm whether Windows adaptive brightness, content adaptive brightness control, or any OEM display utility was enabled at that time, and whether the machine was definitely plugged in.

That will distinguish a Power Display write loop from Windows or OEM brightness automation.

confidence.rationale: Good symptom report, but no diagnostic ZIP yet.
